cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T2 directly: winds need an ocean heat reservoir to carry.
cells.limitation: Geographer turns T3, T6, T9 float free; T3 terrain point never taken up.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4 and T8 sketch a storage versus delivery split.
cells.limitation: Storage/delivery split never developed; T5-T9 mostly repeat opening positions.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Ocean versus atmosphere framed as the core tension from T1-T2.
cells.limitation: Maritime versus continental air, west versus east coasts, Rockies trough never examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 proposes the interaction of ocean and air as the answer.
cells.limitation: T6 interaction claim asserted, not worked out; positions do not reshape each other.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names storage versus transport as the axis of disagreement.
cells.limitation: T9 ends divided with no sharper question than the opening.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 states the Oceanographer's claim accurately before objecting.
cells.limitation: T5 attacks a coastal-localization point the Oceanographer never denied.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the assumption that winds alone supply heat.
cells.limitation: No objection says what breaks if false; T5 is a non sequitur to T4.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T2 correctly credits westerlies with carrying ocean heat onto land.
cells.limitation: T1 conflates Gulf Stream with conveyor belt; T4 overstates; T3 terrain claim vague; six short turns.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T7 narrows to most significant reservoir rather than sole factor.
cells.limitation: T4, T5 state contested claims as fact; Geographer T3, T6 hedge everything.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7: I concede that the current is not the sole factor.
cells.limitation: T7 concession names no cause; Meteorologist never concedes T4's reservoir point.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames the question as ocean versus atmosphere correctly.
cells.limitation: Section E recasts the explanation as a matter of the user's interests.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T9 notes the answer may depend on the coastal region examined.
cells.limitation: Never asks which parts of Canada; mild coastal British Columbia ignored.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section D summarises the competing explanations the user asked about.
cells.limitation: User wanted a why; T9 and Section E leave no explanation standing.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: No invented context; Section A stays within the user's question.
cells.limitation: Scope of comparison (which places, which season) never considered.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E suggests comparing coastal and inland temperature anomalies.
cells.limitation: Which Canadian regions are meant is never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section E contrasts interest in energy budgets with daily weather.
cells.limitation: What the user wants from understanding is never offered as a question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 challenges the popular Gulf-Stream-alone assumption.
cells.limitation: The common Gulf Stream belief is never named as the user's likely assumption.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D separates energy storage from energy transport.
cells.limitation: No examination of what would count as a satisfying explanation.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: No pathologising anywhere in T1-T9.
cells.limitation: Received textbook explanation as outside expectation never surfaced.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T6 invites the user to look at maps themselves.
cells.limitation: T6 offers no distinction the user could accept or reject.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Minds section defines ocean, atmosphere and terrain explanations.
cells.limitation: Terrain explanation in T3 has no stated mechanism.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T8 notes ocean storage needs atmospheric delivery.
cells.limitation: What each explanation costs in evidence is never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: compare coastal versus inland anomalies at the same latitude.
cells.limitation: Section E never says which outcome favours which explanation; ends on user interest.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T9 says the answer may vary by coastal region.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns never separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E coastal-inland comparison is a feasible single step.
cells.limitation: Step is vague: which regions, which data, what result means what.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T2 plain wording: prevailing westerly winds transport that heat.
cells.limitation: T6 the interaction between the two stays abstract.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T8 names the Oceanographer and quotes the claim it answers.
cells.limitation: T6 the two is ambiguous; T3 mountains claim untraceable later.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, each readable at a glance.
cells.limitation: Six turns under 25 words per deterministic checks.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Three disciplines distinct: ocean, atmosphere, terrain.
cells.limitation: T4, T5, T8 share one template; Geographer distinct only by hedging.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are brief and do not pad.
cells.limitation: T8 restates T7 before answering; T9 and Section D recap the split.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T4 sharpens the clash: winds would have no reservoir.
cells.limitation: Tension stays abstract; no vivid contrast like Vancouver versus Labrador.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T7 Oceanographer concedes the current is not the sole factor.
cells.limitation: T7 concession names no earlier argument as cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: Geographer's tentative register in T3 differs slightly.
cells.limitation: All three minds speak in flat textbook register.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T9: whether the sea or the sky is the primary engine.
cells.limitation: T1 conveyor belt is a stock image; no vivid example elsewhere.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T7 concession briefly shifts the exchange.
cells.limitation: Uniform short turns, constant low intensity, no build.

strengths: T2 and T4 frame the core ocean-versus-atmosphere clash directly and responsively.
T4 and T8 hint at a useful storage versus delivery distinction.
Section E proposes an observable coastal-inland comparison the user could look up.
weaknesses: Section E ends on the user's interests rather than which evidence decides between explanations.
Geographer T3, T6, T9 hedge every claim and add no mechanism.
Six turns under 25 words leave every argument thin; nobody develops T4's reservoir point.

symptoms.observed: Section E ties each explanation to user interest, not to an observable outcome.
symptoms.evidence: If you are interested in the global energy budget

symptoms.observed: Never asks which Canadian places; mild west coast unaddressed.
symptoms.evidence: warmer in winter than parts of Canada

symptoms.observed: Geographer hedges every sentence and commits to no mechanism.
symptoms.evidence: perhaps you might find that the mountains in Canada

symptoms.observed: Storage versus delivery split raised but never developed or tested.
symptoms.evidence: atmospheric circulation dictates where that heat actually lands

symptoms.observed: Six turns fall under 25 words, leaving arguments unexplained.
symptoms.evidence: I concede that the current is not the sole factor

findings.description: Six turns under 25 words per deterministic checks.
Claim winds would have no heat reservoir without the current overstates; ocean mixed-layer seasonal storage exists regardless.
Calls Gulf Stream a conveyor belt, a term usually for the overturning circulation; also Section E links ocean to global budget, a loose pairing.
Attributions to Stommel, Lutgens and Tarbuck, and Reclus plausible but positions not checkable here.
Exploratory question ended on which mechanism suits the user's interests.

rubric_fit_notes: Criterion 4 cells on fears and values have little natural purchase for a physical-geography question; rated low for absence of reflective opportunity, with some uncertainty about how harshly that should weigh. misfit_slot is listed for Section E, which has no turn number.
question_type_note: Read as exploratory: criterion 5 judged on evidence that would decide between ocean, atmosphere and terrain explanations, and Section E's interest-based framing cost C3.1 and C5.3.
